builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Are Seismic Foundation Models More Than Glorified Feature Extractors?
summary: This replaces imported audio/vision-style self-supervised objectives (single-window masking or quantization targets) for seismic waveform encoders with a systematic comparison of nine objective/bottleneck/mixer variants on one shared Mamba architecture. The cost is a 3M-window pretraining corpus and a frozen-checkpoint evaluation pipeline, plus the finding that changing the objective redistributes rather than raises downstream skill, so no single checkpoint serves all tasks. Adoption can fail because gains are regime-dependent (few-shot only), masking pressure re-specializes rather than generalizes, and the paper concludes the binding constraint is an occurrence-process learning target that does not yet exist.
rationale: This is a negative-results study specific to seismic waveform modeling with no transferable efficiency or capability technique for a constrained-infrastructure engineer unless their production domain is seismology.
technique: Seismic waveform self-supervised objective comparison (Mamba encoder-decoder)

claims.statement: This replaces imported audio/vision-style self-supervised objectives (single-window masking or quantization targets) for seismic waveform encoders with a systematic comparison of nine objective/bottleneck/mixer variants on one shared Mamba architecture. The cost is a 3M-window pretraining corpus and a frozen-checkpoint evaluation pipeline, plus the finding that changing the objective redistributes rather than raises downstream skill, so no single checkpoint serves all tasks. Adoption can fail because gains are regime-dependent (few-shot only), masking pressure re-specializes rather than generalizes, and the paper concludes the binding constraint is an occurrence-process learning target that does not yet exist.

Masking pressure on the strongest classifier gains 6.9 points of few-shot P-wave picking precision while losing 9.6 points of few-shot classification accuracy; checkpoints beat task-specific baselines few-shot on classification and ground-motion prediction but trail them on full data.
